body_markdown:
Recently, Logitech joined higher education IT, AV, and technology leaders at EDUCAUSE 2026 for conversations about what it takes to support teaching and learning across today’s campuses.


A lot of those conversations came back to a familiar challenge: learning happens across more spaces and formats than ever before. Faculty and students are moving between classrooms, collaboration spaces, content creation environments, and emerging immersive experiences, while IT and AV teams are working to make all of that technology easier to deploy, manage, and use.


That is the idea behind Learning Everywhere, and at EDUCAUSE, Logitech brought it to life across the booth.


**Technology for Different Ways of Teaching and Learning**


Rather than focusing on a single type of campus space, the Logitech booth brought together solutions designed to support a range of higher education experiences.


Attendees explored tools for lecture capture and classroom sharing, including


[Rally Camera Streamline Kit](https://www.logitech.com/en-us/products/video-conferencing/room-solutions/rally-streamline-kit.html) , a camera solution for lecture capture;


[Scribe](https://www.logitech.com/en-us/products/video-conferencing/room-solutions/scribe.html) , which brings whiteboard content into digital sessions; and


[Reach](https://www.logitech.com/en-us/products/education/cameras/reach-camera.html) , a flexible camera for sharing physical materials and demonstrations.


[Rally Board 65](https://www.logitech.com/en-us/products/video-conferencing/room-solutions/rally-board-65.html) showed how an all-in-one collaboration display can support different types of teaching and meeting spaces.


Content creation had a space of its own, with


[Mevo Core](https://www.logitech.com/en-us/shop/p/mevo-core.961-000508) and


[Mevo Start](https://www.logitech.com/en-us/shop/p/mevo-start.961-000498) , compact streaming cameras designed for flexible video capture and live production, paired with Yeti microphones for creating and sharing video and audio content.


The booth also featured


[MX Ink](https://www.logitech.com/en-us/products/vr/mx-ink.html) with Meta Quest for immersive learning experiences, along with


[Spotlight 2](http://logitech.com/en-us/shop/p/spotlight-2-presenter-remote) , Logitech’s advanced presenter designed to help presenters guide attention more clearly with digital highlighting, haptic feedback, and other presentation controls.


Across those experiences, many of the conversations centered on similar priorities: making technology simpler for faculty, creating more consistency across campus, and giving IT and AV teams solutions that can work across different spaces and teaching needs.


**Making Classroom Technology Easier to Use**


Those same themes came through in


[a conversation](https://higheredav.com/hetma-logitech-educause-26/) between Jay Lyons, Product and Portfolio Manager for Education at Logitech, and Higher Ed AV Media live from EDUCAUSE.


During the interview, Jay talked about what Logitech was hearing from higher education institutions at the show. The conversations ranged from what technology makes sense for a particular space to broader questions around interoperability, consistency, and how institutions can scale technology across more of campus.


For faculty, the goal is pretty simple: the technology should support the lesson, not become another thing they have to manage. Jay described a challenge Logitech often sees in higher education: classrooms where complicated instructions and unfamiliar controls can create extra work for instructors. Logitech helps address that challenge with solutions designed to be simpler to use and more consistent from room to room.


**Time with the Higher Education Community**


Some of the best conversations happened outside the booth, too. Logitech hosted a welcome reception with Zoom and others, giving customers, partners, and members of the higher education community another chance to connect after the show floor closed.


EDUCAUSE 2026 reinforced something we hear often in higher education: the best technology is the technology that makes teaching, learning, and support easier.


Thanks to everyone who stopped by the booth, joined the conversation, or spent time with the Logitech team in Denver. We are looking forward to continuing those conversations and bringing what we heard back into how we support higher education.
